A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SD-FM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across page moves.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original ImageNet, PetFace, CelebA super-resolution, guidance, and MeanFlow experiments.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, with additional MeanFlow results and original sensitivity, sampling, cost-ablation, and convergence analyses in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The SD-OT optimization, noise-to-data assignment, flow training, and guidance procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–6. The alternative transport costs are experimental controls; the exact-MIPS description clarifies the existing implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ImageNet at the same image resolutions, PetFace, and CelebA, with the same generation and super-resolution tasks. The added analyses reuse this coverage; smaller models and alternative coupling costs change experimental configurations.

E2.justification: Figures 19–21 add anti-OT and two randomly sign-corrupted transport-cost variants as comparison controls against the standard cost. The established I-FM, OT-FM, and independent MeanFlow comparators remain.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a systematic controlled design crossing transport cost, regularization, and convergence threshold, including fixed random sign masks. Section 5.4 also adds DiT-M/2 trained for 40 epochs alongside the retained 300-epoch XL/2 setting. These substantially expand experimental controls without revising the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's convergence-quality and regularization analyses, Figures 17–23 test potential sensitivity, unequal data sampling, the importance of shortest-path transport costs, interacting threshold/regularization effects, and pixel-versus-latent optimization convergence. This substantially broadens the investigation of why and when SD-FM works.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains its three-seed averaging, and Figure 6 continues to display error bars. No new run-count disclosure, confidence-interval definition, or significance-testing procedure appears. Changed error-bar magnitudes and additional curves concern results.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds M/2 FID curves and modifies some retained XL/2 plotted values and error-bar extents. Figures 17–23 add substantial results on potential sensitivity, sampling imbalance, cost-dependent FID/curvature, and faster latent-space convergence. Tables 2–3 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The assumptions, convergence theorem, generalized Tweedie formula, guidance propositions, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. Changes concern notation, equation references, and typesetting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and efficiency/performance claims. Adding O(N) assignment cost to the abstract repeats information already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly recommends epsilon=0, interprets the cost controls as supporting shortest-path couplings, and attributes easier latent-space optimization to Gaussian-like latent distributions. It also explains how loose convergence thresholds leave images unsampled. These extend the existing interpretation without replacing it.

D1.justification: Section 4 explicitly describes exact MIPS computation, while Appendix F documents fixed-per-experiment sign masks and Figure 18 specifies PCA dimension 1000. The latter conflicts with F.1's full-dimensional description. Existing hardware, Table 4 hyperparameters, and code/access disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 newly states that Genevay et al. (2016) did not consider epsilon=0, sharpening the positioning of the retained convergence analysis. The bibliography contains the same cited works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites, more descriptive experiment headings, standardized equation references, and new appendix sections. The overall narrative remains stable. Editing introduces some roughness: super-resolution evaluation text falls under Guidance, and F.3/F.4 lack explanatory prose.

P2.justification: Seven new figures add potential scatter plots, sampling-count curves, extensive ablation panels, and convergence curves. Figure 6 is enlarged and redesigned for four series. Retained Figures 7–8 are consolidated onto one page, while their plotted content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The cost controls and sampling diagnostics provide useful evidence beyond v1's performance comparisons, and the additional MeanFlow configuration broadens validation. These gains are tempered by incomplete appendix explanations and inconsistent references/captions, including the latent-convergence reference to Figure 18 instead of Figure 23 and Figure 22's epsilon=0 caption despite multiple epsilon settings. The net improvement is useful but limited.
